conviction_note: Findings roughly offset (impact_sum +0.2); the scaled number leans slightly negative (p_up 48 on a 7-point move) because this name's reaction function is asymmetric: the Q2 raise bought +0.56% close-to-close while the Q3 2025 ARR/guide cut cost roughly 14-26%, and the stock goes in at a 52-week high, +8.9% in 20 days, with the FY ARR guide still requiring H2 sequential growth after a Q2 sequential decline. The two measurements differ in sign because the small sourced positives (short base, DocuSign proxy, buyback capacity) are slightly larger than the sourced negatives, while the tail risk sits on the ARR line.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue ~$57.4M and non-GAAP EPS $0.22-0.24: MarketBeat $57.43M / $0.24 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/onespan-nasdaqospn-hits-new-52-week-high-following-better-than-expected-earnings-2026-08-05/, page snapshot 2026-10-29) and Benzinga English $57.4M / $0.22 (via search of https://www.benzinga.com/quote/OSPN/earnings-forecasts); a stale Benzinga-Italian page shows $59.2M / $0.28 and Sidoti cut its (likely GAAP) Q3 EPS to $0.17 from $0.26 on 2026-08-05. The company guide supports the $57.4M figure: FY revenue $248-252M, software & services $202-204M, hardware $46-48M (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm); H1 revenue $126.4M and H1 hardware $22.0M imply H2 software ~$97.6-99.6M and H2 hardware $24-26M, and the CFO put ~1/3 of H2 hardware in Q3, so Q3 ~ $56.8-58.5M (midpoint ~$57.6M). ARR bar: Q2 $189.7M (down from Q1 $192.1M) against FY guide $194-198M.
positioning_check: Short interest 3,450,835 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (~9.4% of shares outstanding), days to cover 7.76, down from a 3,961,679 peak on 2026-09-15 (covering into the rally); source https://equibles.com/stocks/ospn/shortinterest (read 2026-10-29). Option chain unusable: ATM spread 98% of mid, total OI 234; skew +3.68 vol points (downside paid) but not meaningful at that spread. Tape: spot $19.645, prior close ~$20.08 per MarketBeat, 4.6% off the 52-week high, +93.6% off the 52-week low, +8.9% over 20 days, from $15.59 on 2026-08-20.

findings.finding: Q3 ARR is the line under test: ARR fell sequentially from $192.1M (Q1 2026) to $189.7M (Q2 2026, a ~$3M cybersecurity headwind management had flagged), yet the unchanged FY ARR guide of $194-198M needs +$4.3M to +$8.3M in H2; the CFO said on 2026-08-04 he expects sequential ARR increases in both segments in H2 and the CEO said over half of bookings land September to year-end; current deferred revenue fell to $61.3M from $71.6M at year-end (renewal timing, 10-Q) and RPO was $100.0M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time ARR/guide disappointed (Q3 2025, 2025-10-30: ARR guide cut to $183-187M from $186-192M, revenue $57.06M vs $58.18M consensus) the stock fell roughly 14-26% per multiple reports (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1164158150); the Q1 2026 ARR guide raise bought a low-single-digit gain and the Q2 2026 revenue/EBITDA raise +0.56% close-to-close (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The requirement is public, but the stock has rallied ~26% from $15.59 (2026-08-20) to near a 52-week high with no company news in Sep-Oct beyond product releases, which reads as the market assuming the H2 ARR rebuild; if the Q2 sequential dip were being priced as a risk, the stock would not be sitting at the 52-week high into the print. Sign is genuinely uncertain, so sized small with a wide, left-skewed band.
findings.independence: Q1 and Q2 2026 8-K exhibits give the ARR series (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000017/ospnex-991q12026.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm); deferred revenue and RPO from the Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1044777/000104477726000040/ospn-20260630.htm). Same company, different documents; one finding.

findings.finding: EUR/USD fell from 1.1422 (30 June 2026 close) to 1.1330 (30 September 2026 close), -0.8%, and averaged ~1.151 in Q3 2026; with EMEA 35% of revenue (Q2 10-Q), a period-end-rate ARR translation shaves roughly $0.5-1M off reported ARR and a little off reported revenue versus the guide set on 2026-08-04.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance found of this stock reacting to an FX line; management has not cited FX as a driver in the 2026 releases read.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model ARR in USD off the company guide; a sub-1% currency translation is rarely adjusted in estimates for a ~5-analyst name. If priced, consensus ARR would sit below the guide-implied path, and no ARR consensus is visible at all.
findings.independence: Proxy (macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by the company). Geographic mix from the Q2 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1044777/000104477726000040/ospn-20260630.htm.

findings.finding: Guide arithmetic puts Q3 revenue at ~$56.8-58.5M (midpoint ~$57.6M: H2 software & services ~$48.8-49.8M a quarter plus Q3 hardware ~$8.0-8.7M, 1/3 of H2 hardware per the CFO), slightly above the $57.4M consensus; the company beat revenue consensus by ~$2.3M in Q2 ($60.47M vs ~$58.2M) after raising hardware guidance on stronger-than-planned H1 bookings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat plus raise: +0.56% close-to-close (baseline); Q3 2025 revenue miss of 2.2%: roughly -14 to -26%. Beats are bought weakly, misses punished hard.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus sits essentially at the guide-implied midpoint, so this lands inside what the company guided. The residual is the company's habit of beating the midpoint, worth a small amount.
findings.independence: Hardware timing from the call transcript https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-onespan-inc-stock/; consensus from MarketBeat and Benzinga (two agreeing estimate sources).

findings.finding: Overages inflated Q2 Digital Agreements growth to 25% (11.3% excluding overages, per the CFO) and he guided Q3 overages to a 'much smaller level', so headline Digital Agreements growth will optically decelerate from 25% toward ~10% in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of this line moving the stock found.
findings.why_not_priced: The company told the market to expect it, so it is inside guidance; the only residual is a headline-reading algorithm or reader comparing 25% with ~10%.
findings.independence: Same transcript as findings 1 and 3 (different passage). Q2 segment figures in the 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001044777/000104477726000038/ospnex-991q22026.htm.

findings.finding: Short interest is moderately crowded at 3.45M shares (~9.4% of shares outstanding, 7.76 days to cover, 2026-10-15) and has been covered down from 3.96M on 2026-09-15 as the stock rallied; a clean ARR print meets an unfinished short base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze-type reaction visible in the four baseline events (max |move| 3.0%).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fact about the quarter; it changes the reaction function. With 7.8 days to cover, a positive print cannot be absorbed in one session.

findings.finding: Capital return capacity: $47.1M remained on the buyback authorization adopted May 2026 (~6% of a ~$740M market cap) after only $2.9M was used in Q2; the board said it 'will continue to evaluate additional share repurchase opportunities'; dividend $0.13 a quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance of a buyback disclosure moving this stock found.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 repurchase volume is not public until the release; cash was $43.3M with a $100M revolver ($5.0M drawn), so an accelerated Q3 buyback is possible but unconfirmed.
findings.independence: CEO comment on buybacks in the transcript https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-4-onespan-inc-stock/.

findings.finding: Financing: OneSpan had drawn $5.0M on its $100M MUFG revolver at 30 June 2026 after paying $34.6M cash for Build38 in H1; the money funds the acquisition and capital returns, not distress, with adjusted EBITDA guided at $67-71M.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: Build38 and returns, on a profitable company; signed zero.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the capital return finding.

findings.finding: DocuSign, the closest public e-signature peer to the Digital Agreements segment (~32% of OneSpan revenue in Q2), reported on 2026-09-03 for the quarter to July 31: revenue +9% to $875.75M, guided Q3 to $886-890M and raised FY27 revenue guidance; this is after OneSpan last spoke.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No instance found of OSPN reacting to a DocuSign print.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer proxy for a segment whose customers differ (OneSpan sells to banks and regulated enterprises); estimates for OneSpan did not move after it. Sized for what it is, net of the cybersecurity segment (~68% of revenue), which it says nothing about.
findings.independence: Proxy. Same story in DocuSign's own release https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20640567.

findings.finding: Thales, the largest listed competitor in bank authentication and digital identity, reported on 2026-10-22 nine-month Cyber & Digital sales of EUR2,742M, +0.2% organic, with Cyber +2.5% organic and Digital activities slowing: a flat backdrop for security spend in Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: A broad competitor series that lands after OneSpan last spoke; weak transmission to a $60M-a-quarter company, so small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Segment figures via search summary of https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/thales-orders-up-15-over-nine-months-growth-expected-at-top-of-guidance-range/27704.html.

outside_window.finding: OneSpan Sign packaging change between 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-12: new Enterprise-only features (conditional logic, NIGO validation), a new paid SMS notifications add-on, and analytics removed from the compare table; a 2027 monetisation lever with no Q3 effect.
European digital identity wallet regulation requires bank acceptance by end-2027, which management cites as the DigipassONE Verify opportunity; 2027 budgets were not yet clear per the CEO.

baseline_tension: The baseline's skew (+3.68, downside paid) agrees with the slight negative lean, but the chain is too wide to mean anything; the +8.9% 20-day run-up to near a 52-week high raises the bar for the ARR line, and a 9.4% short base with 7.8 days to cover partly offsets it.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range): the revenue-vs-bar finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and the overages finding from -0.3 to -0.1, because both land inside what management guided on 2026-08-04.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): added the $5.0M revolver draw as an explicit financing finding signed 0 after asking what it buys (Build38, buybacks).
Rule 1 / reaction function: Q2's raise bought +0.56% while the Q3 2025 cut cost ~14-26%, so p_up moved from 49 to 48; the findings themselves were not cut again.

Rule 7: short interest was already looked up before any negative; the negatives stay small. Rule 8 / incomplete baseline history (it omits the Oct 2025 print): abs_move_pct kept at 7.0, well above the baseline's 1.89 median.
